article_title: Empowering ChatGPT with guidance mechanism in blended learning: effect of self-regulated learning, higher-order thinking skills, and knowledge construction
citation: Lee, H.-Y., Chen, P.-H., Wang, W.-S., Huang, Y.-M., & Wu, T.-T. (2024). Empowering ChatGPT with guidance mechanism in blended learning: effect of self-regulated learning, higher-order thinking skills, and knowledge construction. International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education, 21, 16. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41239-024-00447-4
title: Guidance-based ChatGPT-assisted Learning Aid (GCLA)
description: The GCLA is an educational tool for blended learning that fuses ChatGPT (the gpt-3.5-turbo-16 k model, max_tokens 4000, temperature 0.6, presence_penalty 0.2) with Apple's Shortcuts on iOS 12+ devices. Its defining behavior is that "Rather than giving direct answers, GCLA prompts students to formulate their own, offering insightful hints to aid problem-solving." Learners must submit a question together with their own proposed answer before receiving guidance, and a learning log file records all questions and answers to support reflection and retention.
requirements: Learners must obtain an OpenAI authentication key and submit their own proposed answer before receiving ChatGPT guidance
Runs on Apple devices with iOS 12 or above via Apple's Shortcuts
constraints: The study's comparison used the GPT-3.5 iteration of ChatGPT on iOS due to its predominant use and use in GCLA's development
examples: In the article's worked example, a student entered a propane combustion problem with an unbalanced initial equation, received a hint that the answer was incorrect, counted atoms, revised to C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O, and had the corrected answer corroborated by the app

article_title: Inclusive and effective teaching of Nature-Based Social Prescribing for allied health professional students within digital environments.
citation: Pywell S., Wallace C., Wallace S., Davies M. (2025). Inclusive and effective teaching of Nature-Based Social Prescribing for allied health professional students within digital environments. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2025.1694834
title: Group Concept Mapping as a coproduction framework for inclusive pedagogy exploration
description: Group Concept Mapping (GCM) is defined in the article as a "structured methodology for organizing the ideas of a group on any topic of interest and presenting those visually through a series of interrelated maps". It integrates participatory, quantitative and qualitative methods: brainstorming generates statements, participants sort and rate them, and multidimensional scaling with Ward's-method hierarchical cluster analysis yields visual theme maps and Go Zone quadrants. The article uses GCM via the groupwisdom tool to coproduce priorities for inclusive NbSP teaching with 38 stakeholders, arguing it frees participants from groupthink constraints of Delphi approaches.
requirements: Anonymous participation and independent stage completion
Sequential mixed methods: sorting before rating
Consolidation of brainstormed statements following published GCM guidance (100-statement maximum)
constraints: Attrition threatens internal validity and must be transparently reported
Results are representative of participants who took part, not generalizable to the wider stakeholder population
Cognitive loading of participants due to task complexity is a known limitation
target_learning_goals: Stakeholder-generated curriculum content priorities for nature-based social prescribing
examples: The study brainstormed 158 statements consolidated to 100, sorted by 10 participants above the 75% threshold, rated by 9, with a stress value of 0.3332 within the reliable 0.21–0.37 range
key_sources: Pywell S., Wallace C., Wallace S., Davies M. (2025). Inclusive and effective teaching of Nature-Based Social Prescribing for allied health professional students within digital environments. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2025.1694834

article_title: Embedding simulation in genetic counselor education from the first week of training: Learning outcomes, standardized clients, and students' satisfaction.
citation: Jacobs, C., & McEwen, A. (2025). Embedding simulation in genetic counselor education from the first week of training: Learning outcomes, standardized clients, and students' satisfaction. Journal of Genetic Counseling, 34, e1857. https://doi.org/10.1002/jgc4.1857
title: Co-designed simulation learning outcomes and standardized clients for genetic counselor education
description: A set of six simulation learning outcomes and eight standardized clients built with experienced genetic counselors using co-design principles for a master of genetic counseling program. The outcomes cover "establishing an effective counseling relationship, eliciting information, assessing need, delivering difficult news and helping clients cope with complex emotions, effective communication and facilitating adaptation". Real cases were de-identified into detailed case studies, mapped to learning outcomes and program stages, and sequenced from straightforward to complex across the two-year program.
requirements: Standardized clients must be reviewed for accuracy, authenticity, and privacy by the genetic counselors involved in the real cases
The authors state regular review and update of the standardized clients is vitally important to optimize learning
constraints: The authors question the extent to which outcomes around communicating effectively and facilitating adaptation can be achieved in a brief simulated interaction
Further work may be needed to validate each standardized client for each learning outcome
target_learners: first-year master of genetic counseling students (novice student genetic counselors)
target_learning_goals: delivering difficult news and helping clients cope with complex emotions
examples: Eight real cases addressing direct-to-consumer testing, variants of uncertain significance, unexpected results, prenatal diagnosis and complex family dynamics were developed into eight standardized clients
The two most straightforward scenarios were selected for the first teaching block
key_sources: Jacobs, C., & McEwen, A. (2025). Embedding simulation in genetic counselor education from the first week of training: Learning outcomes, standardized clients, and students' satisfaction. Journal of Genetic Counseling, 34, e1857. https://doi.org/10.1002/jgc4.1857
